newsitem.title: UK: Regulators call for global controls on insurers.
newsitem.headline: Regulators call for global controls on insurers.

text.p: Insurance companies should be policed globally, U.S. and UK regulators told an insurance conference on Wednesday, but added that worldwide controls will take time to agree and implement.

"Insurance is a global business and will have to be regulated as such," Edward Muhl, superintendent of New York Insurance Department until last year, told a conference organised by the Institute of London Underwriters (ILU) and U.S. law firm Kroll & Tract.
Muhl, who is now executive vice president of Peterson Consulting, said national insurance markets were closely intertwined and regulators were already co-operating.
As an example, he cited opposition in recent years from U.S. investors in Lloyds of London to the insurance market's reconstruction and renewal plan, which was finally agreed last September.

Muhl and Kenneth Gibson, chief deputy commissioner of California Insurance Department, told the conference that they had had to consider the thousands of Lloyd's U.S. policyholders who would have suffered had the market collapsed.
These included airports, transport systems and other public services. A failure of Lloyd's would also have had fatal consequences for many U.S. insurers, they added.
Jonathan Spencer, head of insurance at the UK Department of Trade and Industry (DTI), said national regulators should move towards closer cooperation, but not total harmonisation.
"My own view is that to try to achieve complete harmonisation would be futile, but there are underlying principles and techniques which have widespread applicability."
Countries had adopted different approaches to regulating their insurers, Spencer added.

Britain put the emphasis on company solvency, while Japan concentrated on regulating products. He noted that the U.S. insistence that foreign insurers deposite funds in the U.S. before doing business there was a barrier to free trade.
The International Association of Insurance Supervisors, which will this year set up its own secretariat in Basle, would be a focus for developing a global strategy, Spencer added.
